drills.q: Find the kth largest element in an unsorted array using a heap. State the complexity.
drills.a: Min-heap capped at size k; push each element, pop when size exceeds k; root after processing all elements is the kth largest. O(n log k) time, O(k) space.

drills.q: Why is a min-heap, not a max-heap, correct for finding the K largest elements?
drills.a: The heap holds your current best-k candidates; the root must be the worst of them since that's what gets evicted and what a new element must beat to enter.

drills.q: Derive QuickSelect's average-case time complexity from its recurrence.
drills.a: A random pivot eliminates roughly half the remaining elements on average, and you recurse into only the side containing the target rank: T(n) = T(n/2) + O(n), which sums via geometric series to O(n).

drills.q: Solve Top-K Frequent Elements in O(n) time without sorting the frequency table.
drills.a: Count frequencies with a hashmap, bucket-sort values by frequency into n+1 buckets (frequency is bounded by n), then read the top buckets down until k values are collected.

drills.q: Find the kth smallest element in an n x n matrix sorted ascending along rows and columns, better than flattening and sorting.
drills.a: Min-heap seeded with the first element of each row, pop-and-push the row's next element k times (O(k log n)); or binary search on the value range counting elements <= mid via a staircase walk (O(n log(max-min))).

drills.q: Design a bounded-memory approximate top-10 trending hashtags system over millions of distinct hashtags in a live stream.
drills.a: Replace exact per-hashtag counters with an approximate frequency sketch (Count-Min Sketch or Space-Saving algorithm) to bound memory, and maintain only a small heap of current leading candidates rather than exact counts for every key ever seen.
